alignments.note: Postpositive δέ realized by the ASV's clause-initial Now.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun he and nothing else, the ASV writing two English words for the pair, so rule 90's one-word case does not arise.
The participle carries the supplied relativizer that under rules 7 and 32; head on the lexical verb under rule 17.
Governed pronoun stands on its own English word (rule 2).
εἰς rendered in; the preposition governing the phrase takes the English preposition under rule 36 rather than being absorbed into establisheth.
Coordinating conjunction joining the two participles; expressed in Greek, so rule 88's supplied juncture is not in question.
Second participle rendered by a bare past form under the shared he that; no separate helper is written for it.
Second object pronoun, kept distinct from s004 under rule 2.

Verbless clause: the supplied copula rides with the predicate noun under rule 53's main principle, since rule 32 lets the substantival article supply the pronoun and nothing else. Rule 92's ὁ κύριός → he who is … Master at EPH.6.9 is the same configuration and puts the copula on the predicate noun. Rule 53's subject-pronoun exception for a noun-phrase predicate is the competing reading, which would give the discontinuous he … is to s001; rule 68 extends that exception to a substantival demonstrative, so extending it to a pronoun-supplying article stays defensible.

review_notes: Reviewed; returned unchanged apart from note wording. Partition checked: s001–s012 and t001–t014 each used exactly once, every head a member of its array.
s001/s003 split follows rule 32 (οἱ κατοικοῦντες → they that dwell), not rule 90, because the ASV writes two English words for the article-plus-participle pair.
s012's copula placement is the only genuinely contested unit; kept medium with the competing rule 53 reading named, and rule 92's EPH.6.9 precedent added as the support for the accepted reading.
εἰς → in kept on the preposition rather than absorbed into establisheth (rule 36).
καί is expressed, so and is aligned to s009 in the ordinary way; rule 88's supplied-juncture question does not arise, and χρίσας takes no second relativizer because the ASV writes none.
